text.tspan: A packet's journey: going out (MASQUERADE) and coming in (DNAT)
not for me, so send it out of eth0
the internet can't reply to it
so the reply comes back here
Red row = the only place an address changes. MASQUERADE changes FROM (going out); DNAT changes TO (coming in).
Replies travel the same path backwards: conntrack remembers each change and reverses it automatically.
Only the first packet of a connection hits the NAT rule; conntrack handles the rest.
